newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends slightly up on BOK intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends slightly up on BOK intervention.

text.p: The won recouped losses to finish slightly higher on Wednesday after central bank intervention pulled it up from six-year lows, dealers said.
"The central bank began selling dollars in the morning when the won hit a six-year low of 830.30. It intervened at least two more times later," said a dealer with a foreign bank.
The won closed at 829.50 after opening at 829.70. It ranged from 829.10 to 830.30.
Dealers said upward pressure on the dollar remained strong due to rising dollar demand for importer settlements.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 829.10 on Thursday, compared with 808.20 today.
"As the nation's exports have become sluggish, demand for the dollar is expected to remain strong," said a dealer with a domestic bank.
Dealers said expectations for a further rise in the dollar prompted an outflow of dollar funds in South Korea.
"Given the dollar's rise, alomost no one will want to hold the won in place of the dollar," he said.
